# One mark, two targets, both folded

A mark carrying both `see=` and `see-also=` renders its targets through a
command of its own rather than through the single-target encapsulation, which
is the third place a target is rendered and so the third place a fold has to
reach. Both targets here name entries this file marks at overflow depth, so
neither dangles and the only thing under test is whether each one prints the
path its entry prints.

It lives apart from `fold-xref.qmd` because its printed index row carries two
whole folded paths and both labels, which no index column can hold without
wrapping — and a wrapped row is not something the printed-index check can read.

The entries: [oat]{.index entry="Oat!Pea!Rye!Soy"} and
[tef]{.index entry="Tef!Urd!Vet!Wid!Xan"}.

The mark naming both: [yuc]{.index entry="Yuc" see="Oat!Pea!Rye!Soy"
see-also="Tef!Urd!Vet!Wid!Xan"}.

::: {.qi-index-here}
